raw_response:
I’ll keep most of my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because on a small place like mine I cannot take big risks. I have 4.1 mu total, so I will put about 2.6 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and keep 1.5 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize are still my safer income, and cotton gives me another leg to stand on if grain price is not so good. I only finished middle school, so I don’t calculate everything very finely. I mostly go by what worked on my own fields and what the better farmers nearby are doing. Last year the wheat did better when I split the fertilizer instead of putting too much at once, so I will do that again.

Cash still matters to me, even if my family has several people. Some work off-farm, so labor is not always free when I need it. I have well irrigation, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless the crop really needs it. For wheat I would rather not be stingy with fertilizer, because if the stand turns yellow I lose yield fast. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I will keep it simple and sow quickly with light tillage or direct seeding. Cotton takes more watching for insects and more hand labor at picking, so I keep only a smaller area in it.
